IssueArea of focusRelevant guidance
Strategy pillar
Fail to consider broader climate-related risks affecting the organisationGather experts from different fields (for example: finance, risk and sustainability) to effectively consider the wide array of climate-related risks.NAO insights UK Climate Change Risk Assessment
Consider both direct and indirect risks.
Fail to consider the potential financial impacts of climate risksConsider quantum of climate risks and opportunities — from physical hazards and policy or market transitions — to inform decisions. Weigh up costs of inaction against adaptation benefits, factoring in uncertainty and time horizons, and use economic and scenario analysis to guide sustainable investment and capital allocation.Monetary Valuation of Risk and Opportunity
Metrics and Targets pillar
Incomplete emissions results due to inappropriate reporting boundariesOrganisations may need to set emissions reporting boundaries beyond those in the GGCs where material sources are omitted. GGC reporting alone may be insufficient if it excludes significant scopes or sources the organisation monitors and manages (or should be). In such cases, boundaries should be reassessed and additional emissions calculated to capture all relevant activities. Where reporting extends beyond GGC scope, the methodology — including any Scope 3 estimation techniques — must be disclosed.Appendix A - Sustainability Reporting Concepts, Principles and Foundations See Reporting Boundaries
